## Sentiment over Time

```{r time-data, include=FALSE}
weekly_all <- scores |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarise(net = mean(bert_net), se = sd(bert_net) / sqrt(n()), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= MIN_WEEK_N)

weekly_country <- scores |>
  group_by(country, week) |>
  summarise(net = mean(bert_net), var = var(bert_net), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# 7-day rolling mean over calendar days, weighted by articles: each day's value is the
# mean of all articles in that day and the six before it; shown only with >= 5 articles.
roll7 <- function(x) as.numeric(stats::filter(x, rep(1, 7), sides = 1))
rolling <- scores |>
  filter(country %in% large_countries) |>
  group_by(country, published_date) |>
  summarise(sum_net = sum(bert_net), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(country, published_date = seq(min(published_date), max(published_date), by = "day"),
           fill = list(sum_net = 0, n = 0)) |>
  arrange(country, published_date) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  mutate(n7 = roll7(n), net7 = ifelse(n7 >= 5, roll7(sum_net) / n7, NA_real_)) |>
  ungroup()

rolling_all <- scores |>
  group_by(published_date) |>
  summarise(sum_net = sum(bert_net), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(published_date = seq(min(published_date), max(published_date), by = "day"),
           fill = list(sum_net = 0, n = 0)) |>
  arrange(published_date) |>
  mutate(n7 = roll7(n), net7 = ifelse(n7 >= 5, roll7(sum_net) / n7, NA_real_))

f2n <- function(x) sub("^-", "−", sprintf("%.2f", x))
lo_week <- slice_min(weekly_all, net, n = 1)
hi_week <- slice_max(weekly_all, net, n = 1)
```

### Weekly net sentiment, all sources

```{r weekly-all, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=10}
ggplot(weekly_all, aes(x = week, y = net)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = net - 1.96 * se, ymax = net + 1.96 * se), fill = "#4472C4", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "#4472C4", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = "#4472C4") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, name = "Articles") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%d %b") +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly mean net sentiment, all sources pooled",
    subtitle = paste0("Shaded band = 95% confidence interval; weeks with at least ", MIN_WEEK_N, " articles"),
    x = NULL, y = "Net sentiment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

Weekly means range from `r f2n(lo_week$net)` (week of `r format(lo_week$week, "%e %B")`) to
`r f2n(hi_week$net)` (week of `r format(hi_week$week, "%e %B")`, `r hi_week$n` articles). From
the late-February escalation onwards they settle around −0.60 with narrow bands. Busier weeks
tend to be more negative (correlation `r f2n(cor(weekly_all$n, weekly_all$net))` across the
`r nrow(weekly_all)` weeks shown), which with so few points is suggestive at most.

### 7-day rolling net sentiment by country

```{r rolling, fig.height=7, fig.width=12}
rolling |>
  ggplot(aes(x = published_date, y = net7)) +
  geom_line(data = rolling_all |> select(-any_of("country")), color = "grey70",
            linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(color = "#1976D2", linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~country, ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(
    title = "7-day rolling mean of net sentiment by country",
    subtitle = paste0("Calendar days, article-weighted, shown when the window holds at least 5 articles; ",
                      "grey = all sources pooled. Countries with at least 100 articles."),
    x = NULL, y = "Net sentiment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Gaps mark stretches with fewer than five articles in seven days, which covers much of January
and February outside Israel, the UK and Al Jazeera. From March onwards Germany and Israel stay
above the pooled line, while the UK, the USA and Al Jazeera run slightly below it, the same
order as in the country averages.

### Weekly net sentiment per outlet

```{r small-multiples, fig.height=12, fig.width=14}
scores |>
  add_count(outlet_name, name = "outlet_n") |>
  filter(outlet_n >= MIN_OUTLET_N) |>
  group_by(country, outlet_name, week) |>
  summarise(net = mean(bert_net), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 3) |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(outlet_name, " (", country, ")")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = net)) +
  geom_col(width = 6, fill = "#D32F2F") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", limits = range(scores$week) + c(-4, 4)) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly mean net sentiment per outlet",
    subtitle = paste0("Outlets with at least ", MIN_OUTLET_N,
                      " articles; weeks with at least 3 articles; same time axis in every panel"),
    x = NULL, y = "Net sentiment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

No outlet is net positive in any week. Most outlets only reach three articles a week from late
February, so the early bars come mainly from the Israeli and British outlets and Al Jazeera.

### Week-to-week volatility

The spread of weekly means mixes real change with sampling noise: a week with few articles
has a noisy mean. The chart compares the observed spread with the spread that noise alone
would produce.

```{r volatility, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=8}
volatility <- weekly_country |>
  filter(n >= MIN_WEEK_N) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  filter(n() >= 6) |>
  summarise(
    observed = sd(net),
    noise    = sqrt(mean(var / n)),
    weeks    = n(),
    articles = sum(n),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

lim <- c(0, max(c(volatility$observed, volatility$noise)) * 1.1)
volatility |>
  ggplot(aes(x = noise, y = observed, label = country)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = articles), color = "#1976D2", alpha = 0.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 4) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Articles") +
  coord_equal(xlim = lim, ylim = lim) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed week-to-week spread vs. sampling noise",
    subtitle = paste0("SD of weekly means; weeks with at least ", MIN_WEEK_N,
                      " articles,\ncountries with 6+ such weeks. Above the line = more\nmovement than sampling noise explains"),
    x = "Expected SD from sampling noise alone", y = "Observed SD of weekly means"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

```{r volatility-numbers, include=FALSE}
vr <- mutate(volatility, ratio = observed / noise)
above <- filter(vr, ratio > 1)
below <- filter(vr, ratio <= 1)
```

`r nrow(above)` of the `r nrow(vr)` countries move more than sampling noise alone would
produce, by a factor of `r sprintf("%.1f", min(above$ratio))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(above$ratio))`, with `r above$country[which.max(above$ratio)]` the most
changeable. `r paste(below$country, collapse = " and ")`'s weekly means vary less than noise
would predict, but with only `r paste(below$weeks, collapse = "/")` weeks of enough articles.
